The collar unit device includes a receiving cavity configured to receive and support a metal electrode probe. The metal electrode probe is positioned within the receiving cavity in a manner that allows it to respond to vibrations produced by acoustic events.

At least one elastomeric ring encircles the metal electrode probe. The elastomeric ring provides mechanical isolation between the metal electrode probe and the surrounding structure of the receiving cavity. This isolation helps reduce unwanted mechanical interference while allowing the probe to detect relevant vibrations more accurately.

A grommet component is provided to secure a piezoelectric element within the collar unit device. The grommet holds the piezoelectric element in a fixed position so that the piezoelectric element remains in contact with the metal electrode probe. Maintaining this contact allows vibrations detected by the metal electrode probe to be transferred effectively to the piezoelectric element.

During operation, the metal electrode probe detects vibrations associated with acoustic events. These vibrations are transmitted through the metal electrode probe to the piezoelectric element. In response to the received vibrations, the piezoelectric element generates an electrical signal that is proportional to the frequency and magnitude of the vibrations.

The generated electrical signal is received by at least one processor of the collar unit device. The processor processes the signal to evaluate characteristics of the detected acoustic event, such as its vibration frequency, amplitude, or other related parameters.
outputs.L4:
A collar unit device is provided for detecting acoustic-event vibrations and converting those vibrations into electrical signals suitable for analysis by an electronic processor. The device includes a housing or collar body that supports a metal electrode probe positioned to receive mechanical vibrations produced by an acoustic event. The probe may be arranged so that it contacts, or is placed in close mechanical communication with, a surface or structure through which the vibrations travel.

The metal electrode probe is mechanically isolated from portions of the collar unit by one or more elastomeric rings. These rings support the probe while reducing unwanted mechanical coupling between the probe and the surrounding housing. By limiting the transfer of extraneous vibrations and damping non-relevant mechanical noise, the elastomeric rings help improve the sensitivity and reliability of acoustic-event detection. The rings may also help maintain the probe in a desired position while allowing sufficient movement for vibration transfer.

The probe is mechanically coupled to a piezoelectric element. The piezoelectric element is secured within the collar unit by a grommet, which holds the element in place while permitting effective transmission of vibration energy from the probe. The grommet may also provide additional isolation, cushioning, and alignment, thereby protecting the piezoelectric element from excessive mechanical stress while preserving the responsiveness of the sensing assembly.

During operation, vibrations associated with an acoustic event are received by the metal electrode probe. The probe transfers these vibrations to the piezoelectric element. In response to the mechanical deformation caused by the vibrations, the piezoelectric element produces electrical signals. The characteristics of these signals correspond to the frequency, amplitude, and magnitude of the detected vibrations.

The generated electrical signals are provided to processing circuitry associated with the collar unit. The processor may analyze the signals to identify vibration patterns, determine whether an acoustic event has occurred, and distinguish relevant events from background noise or incidental movement. By evaluating signal strength, frequency content, timing, and other measurable parameters, the collar unit can detect acoustic events with improved accuracy.

This configuration allows the collar unit to function as a compact vibration-based acoustic sensor. The combination of the metal electrode probe, elastomeric isolation rings, piezoelectric element, and securing grommet provides a mechanically stable sensing structure that is responsive to acoustic-event vibrations while reducing interference from unwanted mechanical disturbances.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it plays a very important role. It is called the definite article, and it helps us speak about something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we may mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we are talking about a particular book that the listener or reader can identify.

This simple word gives clarity and direction to communication. It can point to something already mentioned, something unique, or something known by everyone. Phrases like “the sun,” “the world,” and “the future” feel complete because “the” guides our attention to one clear idea.

Although it is often overlooked, “the” is essential in everyday English. It connects thoughts, sharpens meaning, and helps sentences sound natural. Without it, many expressions would feel incomplete or confusing. In this way, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have great importance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style device description for a collar-mounted acoustic sensor that uses a metal electrode probe, elastomeric isolation rings, a piezoelectric element, a grommet, and a processor to detect and process vibration events.
counterfactuals.output:
A collar-mounted acoustic sensing device comprises a housing configured for attachment to, or integration with, an animal collar. The device is configured to detect vibration events transmitted through or associated with the collar, the animal, or an object contacting the collar, and to generate corresponding electrical signals for processing.

In one embodiment, the device includes a metal electrode probe extending at least partially through an opening in the housing. The metal electrode probe is arranged to receive mechanical vibration energy from an external source and to conduct the vibration energy toward an internal sensing assembly. The probe may be formed from stainless steel, brass, aluminum, or another conductive metal suitable for mechanical coupling and electrical connection. A distal end of the probe may be exposed outside the housing, while a proximal end may be positioned within the housing in contact with, adjacent to, or otherwise mechanically coupled to a piezoelectric element.

The piezoelectric element is disposed within the housing and is configured to convert mechanical vibrations received from the metal electrode probe into an electrical signal. The piezoelectric element may comprise a piezoelectric ceramic, piezoelectric polymer, piezoelectric disc, piezoelectric bimorph, or other vibration-responsive transducer. In some embodiments, the metal electrode probe also functions as an electrical electrode for the piezoelectric element, thereby providing both mechanical coupling and electrical signal conduction.

One or more elastomeric isolation rings are positioned around the metal electrode probe, the piezoelectric element, or both. The elastomeric isolation rings may be formed from silicone, rubber, thermoplastic elastomer, polyurethane, or another resilient material. The isolation rings are configured to mechanically suspend or isolate the sensing assembly from the housing, thereby attenuating unwanted vibration, impact noise, collar movement artifacts, or housing-borne disturbances. The elastomeric isolation rings may further provide sealing, centering, strain relief, or shock absorption for the metal electrode probe.

A grommet is positioned at an interface between the metal electrode probe and the housing. The grommet may surround a portion of the probe and may be configured to retain the probe in a desired position, prevent ingress of moisture or debris, and reduce transmission of non-target vibration modes from the housing to the probe. The grommet may be formed from an elastomeric material and may cooperate with the isolation rings to define a compliant mounting structure for the probe and piezoelectric element.

The piezoelectric element is electrically coupled to a processor disposed within the housing. The processor is configured to receive one or more electrical signals generated by the piezoelectric element in response to detected vibration events. The processor may include, or be coupled to, signal-conditioning circuitry such as a charge amplifier, voltage amplifier, impedance-matching circuit, analog filter, analog-to-digital converter, or transient protection circuit. The processor may execute instructions stored in memory to process the electrical signals and determine whether a detected vibration event corresponds to a predetermined event type.

In operation, a vibration event is mechanically coupled to the metal electrode probe. The probe transmits the vibration to the piezoelectric element, which generates an electrical output representative of the vibration. The elastomeric isolation rings and grommet reduce undesired mechanical coupling from the housing and collar while allowing desired vibration energy to be transmitted through the probe. The processor receives the electrical output and performs one or more processing operations, including amplification, filtering, sampling, threshold detection, frequency analysis, pattern recognition, event counting, duration measurement, or classification.

The processor may distinguish vibration events based on one or more parameters, including amplitude, frequency content, rise time, decay time, pulse width, repetition rate, energy level, spectral signature, or correlation with stored event profiles. In certain embodiments, the processor identifies events such as scratching, tapping, impact, vocalization-related vibration, collar manipulation, animal movement, or environmental contact. Upon detecting a qualifying event, the processor may store event data, generate an alert, transmit a wireless signal, update a behavioral log, or trigger another device function.

The housing may further include a power source, memory, wireless communication circuitry, and one or more user-interface elements. The power source may comprise a rechargeable battery or replaceable cell. The wireless communication circuitry may communicate processed event information to a remote device, such as a smartphone, base station, or cloud-connected system.

In some embodiments, the metal electrode probe, elastomeric isolation rings, piezoelectric element, and grommet are arranged along a common longitudinal axis to form a compact vibration-sensing stack. In other embodiments, the piezoelectric element is laterally offset from the probe and mechanically coupled through an intermediate conductive member. The elastomeric isolation rings may be compressed between the housing and the probe or between the housing and a support carrier for the piezoelectric element, thereby tuning the sensitivity and frequency response of the acoustic sensing device.

The described structure provides a collar-mounted acoustic sensor capable of selectively detecting vibration events while reducing false detections caused by broad housing vibration or collar motion. The combination of a metal electrode probe, compliant elastomeric isolation, a piezoelectric conversion element, a sealing grommet, and electronic processing enables compact and robust vibration sensing suitable for wearable collar applications.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a formal invention summary for a collar unit device that detects acoustic events via a metal electrode probe transferring vibrations to a piezoelectric element, which outputs an electrical signal to a processor.
counterfactuals.output:
## Invention Summary

The invention relates to a collar unit configured for detecting acoustic events associated with an animal, person, or monitored subject. The collar unit includes a housing carried by or coupled to a collar or similar wearable support structure. The housing contains a vibration-sensitive sensing assembly arranged to detect sound or acoustic energy through mechanical coupling rather than solely through an air microphone.

In one embodiment, the sensing assembly includes a metal electrode probe positioned to contact, engage, or be mechanically coupled to a surface of the monitored subject or to a portion of the collar structure. Acoustic events, including vocalizations, impacts, breathing-related sounds, chewing sounds, coughing, barking, or other body-transmitted or collar-transmitted vibrations, are received by the metal electrode probe as mechanical vibrations. The metal electrode probe transfers the received vibrations to a piezoelectric element mechanically coupled to the probe.

The piezoelectric element converts the transferred mechanical vibrations into an electrical signal representative of the detected acoustic event. The electrical signal is provided to an electronic processing circuit, which may include one or more of an amplifier, filter, analog-to-digital converter, microcontroller, digital signal processor, memory, wireless communication module, or power management circuitry. The processor analyzes the electrical signal to identify, classify, store, or transmit information corresponding to the detected acoustic event.

The collar unit may be configured to distinguish target acoustic events from background noise by processing features of the signal generated by the piezoelectric element, such as amplitude, frequency content, duration, waveform pattern, spectral characteristics, or temporal repetition. Because the metal electrode probe mechanically transfers vibrations to the piezoelectric element, the collar unit may provide improved detection of acoustic events occurring at or near the subject while reducing sensitivity to ambient airborne noise.

In some implementations, the metal electrode probe may also serve as an electrical contact, structural coupling member, or sensing interface. The probe may be formed from stainless steel, brass, conductive alloy, or another durable conductive material suitable for contact with skin, fur, fabric, or collar components. The piezoelectric element may be mounted within the housing so that vibration energy received by the probe is efficiently transmitted to the piezoelectric element while protecting the sensing assembly from moisture, shock, and environmental contaminants.

The invention thereby provides a wearable collar-based acoustic detection device in which mechanical vibrations are captured by a metal electrode probe, converted by a piezoelectric element into an electrical signal, and processed by onboard electronics to detect and evaluate acoustic events.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the components and operation of a wearable collar device for sensing animal vocalizations or acoustic events, including a probe, elastomeric rings, piezo sensor, retaining grommet, and signal-processing processor.
counterfactuals.output:
A wearable collar device for sensing animal vocalizations or other acoustic events can be built as a collar-mounted acoustic pickup that mechanically couples vibrations from the animal’s neck or throat area to an electronic sensor.

The device may include the following components:

- **Collar or wearable support:**  
  A strap or collar is worn around the animal’s neck and supports the sensing assembly in a stable position.

- **Probe:**  
  A probe extends from the collar toward, or into contact with, the animal’s neck. The probe receives mechanical vibrations caused by vocalizations, swallowing, breathing, coughing, chewing, or other acoustic events. It acts as a vibration-transmitting member between the animal and the sensor.

- **Elastomeric rings:**  
  One or more elastomeric rings are positioned around the probe or within the probe mounting structure. These rings provide compliant support, allowing the probe to move in response to acoustic vibrations while reducing unwanted mechanical noise from collar motion. They may also help isolate the sensor from impacts, rubbing, or gross movement of the collar.

- **Piezoelectric sensor:**  
  A piezo sensor is mechanically coupled to the probe so that vibrations transmitted through the probe stress or flex the piezoelectric element. The piezoelectric sensor converts those mechanical vibrations into an electrical signal corresponding to the sensed vocalization or acoustic event.

- **Retaining grommet:**  
  A retaining grommet holds the probe, elastomeric rings, and/or piezo sensor in the desired alignment within the collar housing. The grommet may also provide sealing, strain relief, vibration isolation, and mechanical retention so that the sensing assembly remains properly positioned during animal movement.

- **Signal-processing processor:**  
  Electrical signals from the piezo sensor are routed to a processor or signal-processing circuit. The processor may amplify, filter, digitize, and analyze the signal to detect events such as barking, growling, whining, chewing, coughing, or other acoustic patterns. It may compare signal amplitude, frequency content, duration, repetition rate, or other features against stored thresholds or classification models.

In operation, when the animal produces a vocalization or acoustic event, vibrations propagate through the animal’s neck tissue and into the probe. The elastomeric rings permit controlled movement of the probe while damping non-relevant mechanical disturbances. The probe transfers the vibration to the piezoelectric sensor, which generates a corresponding electrical signal. The retaining grommet keeps the sensor assembly mechanically stable and properly coupled. The processor then conditions and analyzes the signal to identify the type, timing, or intensity of the vocalization or acoustic event. The processed information may be stored, transmitted wirelessly, used to trigger feedback, or used for health and behavior monitoring.

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following concept into patent application language: a collar housing has a cavity receiving a metal electrode probe, rubber rings isolate the probe, the probe contacts a piezoelectric element secured by a grommet, and the piezoelectric signal is processed electronically.
counterfactuals.output:
A device comprising a collar housing defining an internal cavity, a metallic electrode probe disposed at least partially within the internal cavity, and one or more elastomeric ring members positioned between the metallic electrode probe and the collar housing to electrically and/or mechanically isolate the metallic electrode probe from the collar housing. The metallic electrode probe is arranged to engage, contact, or otherwise transmit force to a piezoelectric element retained relative to the collar housing by a grommet. The piezoelectric element is configured to generate an electrical signal in response to mechanical input received through the metallic electrode probe. Electronic circuitry is operatively coupled to the piezoelectric element and configured to receive, condition, process, amplify, filter, digitize, or otherwise evaluate the electrical signal generated by the piezoelectric element.

In one embodiment, the collar housing includes a probe-receiving bore or cavity dimensioned to receive the metallic electrode probe in an axially aligned relationship. The elastomeric ring members may comprise rubber O-rings disposed around the metallic electrode probe to provide sealing, vibration damping, electrical isolation, centering, or mechanical spacing between the metallic electrode probe and the collar housing. The grommet may be formed from an elastomeric or insulating material and may secure the piezoelectric element in a predetermined position such that mechanical pressure, vibration, impact, or displacement applied to the metallic electrode probe is transferred to the piezoelectric element. The electronic circuitry may include one or more of an impedance matching circuit, charge amplifier, voltage amplifier, filter, analog-to-digital converter, microcontroller, signal processor, threshold detector, transmitter, or output interface for producing a processed output corresponding to the piezoelectric signal.
